claims: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
NASA's Artemis II mission launch location is Launch Complex 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
NASA's Artemis II mission has a 2-hour launch window.
NASA's Artemis II mission duration is approximately 10 days.
The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
NASA's Artemis II mission is a crewed mission that will send four astronauts around the Moon.
Live coverage of NASA's Artemis II mission starts on NASA's YouTube channel at 7:45 a.m. EDT.
If the Artemis II launch is delayed, backup opportunities are available within a 5-day window.
Artemis II backup launch opportunities potentially last until April 6, 2026.
NASA's Artemis II mission will test the Orion capsule's life-support systems.
NASA's Artemis II mission will test the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule's life-support systems in preparation for future lunar landings.
